why.comeback: Bankrupt 2015 (EUR 218m debts), refounded in Serie D with fans holding 25%; three straight promotions to Serie A by 2018; relegated 2021, back 2024.
why.punch: Krause investment since 2020; 16th in 2024-25 and 13th in 2025-26, about what the money buys.

why.comeback: Steady rise from amateur levels under Mapei; one relegation (2024) followed by an immediate Serie B title.
why.punch: Small-town club, 6th in 2016 and 8th twice under De Zerbi, strong player sales; relegated 2024, 11th in 2025-26 on a mid budget.

why.comeback: Defined by the 1949 Superga disaster; bankrupt in 2005 and refounded in Serie B, promoted 2006 and again 2012 after another relegation.
why.punch: Mid-table (9th-12th) for five seasons on a mid budget; long fan protests over lack of ambition under Cairo.

why.comeback: Points deduction and relegation in 1986-87 are distant; in Serie A without a break since 1995-96.
why.punch: Pozzo scouting network long sold well; last five seasons lower mid-table survival (10th in 2025-26) on a lower-half budget.

why.comeback: Bankrupt three times (2005, 2009, 2015), refounded in Serie D in 2009 and 2015; climbed to Serie A in 2021 and won Serie B in 2026.
why.punch: Yo-yo since 2021: relegated from Serie A in 2022 and 2025; spends at the top of Serie B, promoted on that money.

why.comeback: Double winners 1996, relegated 2012 after 32 top-flight seasons; ten years in Ligue 2, back 2022, down 2023, Ligue 2 champions 2024.
why.punch: Small budget; stayed up in Ligue 1 in 2024-25 and 2025-26 (15th). Estimate on budget rank.

why.comeback: Relegated 2011 and bottom of Ligue 2 when Rybolovlev bought the club; promoted 2013, champions 2017.
why.punch: Large budget plus tax advantage; 3rd 2021, 2nd 2024, 7th 2026; strong sales model but results match resources.

why.comeback: Ordinary ups and downs: promoted 2015, relegated 2023, back in 2024.
why.punch: One of the smaller budgets, lower mid-table (13th in 2025-26); two FIFA transfer bans (2021, 2023).

why.comeback: Liquidated in 1991 and dropped to amateur football; climbed back to Ligue 2 in 2004, Ligue 1 in 2010 and 2019.
why.punch: One of Ligue 1's smallest budgets, 3rd in 2023-24 and a Champions League knockout play-off in 2025.

why.comeback: France's oldest club spent 2009-2023 in Ligue 2 before winning it in 2023; no near-death episode found.
why.punch: Among the smallest Ligue 1 budgets, has stayed up three seasons running (14th in 2025-26); known academy. Estimate on budget.

why.comeback: Liquidated in 2013 and restarted in the regional amateur league; climbed back to Ligue 2 in 2019 and 2025 and to Ligue 1 in 2026.
why.punch: Two promotions in two seasons (2025, 2026); new OutField investors since 2025. Budget rank is an estimate.

why.comeback: Relegated 2008 and 2011; 2014 promotion annulled by the DNCG in 2015; five more years in Ligue 2 before returning in 2020.
why.punch: Mid-sized budget, 2nd in 2023 and 2026 and the 2026 Coupe de France, with a clear coaching identity.

why.comeback: Near relegation in 2018 and an owner debt crisis around 2020 (lender took control); won the title in 2021 regardless.
why.punch: Ligue 1 title 2021 and regular Europe on a budget far below PSG's; CIES ranks its transfer balance among the world's best.

why.comeback: Bankrupt in 1978 (fans kept the name) and 1990, both distant; recent history is relegations (2017, 2024) and quick returns.
why.punch: Small budget, yo-yo between Ligue 1 and Ligue 2; 10th in 2025-26 after promotion.

why.comeback: Seven straight titles to 2008, then decline; Textor's debts led to a DNCG relegation in June 2025, overturned on appeal; Kang bought the club out of administration in 2026.
why.punch: High budget but 6th, 6th and 4th in recent seasons; debt and ownership turmoil.

why.comeback: Stripped of the 1993 title and relegated in 1994 over match fixing, back in 1996; no deep crisis since.
why.punch: Second-largest revenue in France with heavy losses; 2nd twice, no trophy since 2012.

why.comeback: Administratively relegated by the DNCG in 2002, reversed on appeal; otherwise ordinary ups and downs.
why.punch: INEOS spending since 2019; 5th in 2024, then 16th and a relegation play-off in 2026; club for sale.

why.comeback: Long decline after the 1972 split from PSG, decades in the lower and amateur leagues; promoted to Ligue 1 in 2025 for the first time since 1979.
why.punch: Arnault-family money since 2024; 11th in the first Ligue 1 season, about what the budget buys.

why.comeback: Financial trouble and a near relegation in 2008 before the 2011 Qatar takeover; nothing that defines the club now.
why.punch: By far the largest budget in France; Champions League 2025 and 2026 bought with that money.

why.comeback: Near bankruptcy in 1978 is distant; stable under Pinault since 1998.
why.punch: Top-five budget in France with a strong academy; 4th twice, then 10th and 12th, 6th in 2025-26.

why.comeback: Bankrupt in 2011 and restarted in the fifth tier; four promotions to return to Ligue 1 in 2017, now in Europe.
why.punch: BlueCo's heavy spending on young players since 2023; 7th in 2025 and a Conference League semi-final in 2026.

why.comeback: Bankrupt in 2001 and sent to the third tier; relegated again in 2020, Ligue 2 champions in 2022.
why.punch: RedBird's data-led model on a modest budget: Coupe de France 2023, Europa League 2023-24, mid-table since.

why.comeback: Bankruptcies and refounding in the 1970s-80s are distant; recent yo-yo, double relegation in 2024, Ligue 2 champions 2026.
why.punch: City Football Group backing since 2020, yet relegated in 2023 and down to the third tier in 2024.

why.comeback: Administration in 1992, owner arrested in 2011 and receivership, 9-point deduction in 2019, relegated to League One in 2024; promoted back as champions in 2025.
why.punch: Knighthead's record League One spending to go up; 10th in the 2025-26 Championship.
